questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
First of all I was intrigued by the program: "Construcción de Paz", and I always wanted to go back to South America with my studies. Prior to the exchange I did not have any personal ties to Colombia, but many people around the world had recommended me to go. 
In addition,  I was curious to delve into the anthropological discipline and hoped to find a place and a theme for my Master's Project, which I think I did.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Demanding, but excellent professors! I absolutely loved the content of the program, and  the study environment was also vibrant with dedicated students who were more than willing to share their experiences and perspectives on the subjects as well as on life. 
Bogota was an interesting city with a lot of culture, but leaving the capital to undertake some preliminary fieldwork after the exams Colombia opened itself to me. I definitely hope to go back sooner rather than later!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The staff at the the international office was very attentive to our needs. All international students received all the information regarding inscription, visa regulations, housing, etc. in due time. They even managed to respond to e-mails within 48 hours, and also opened a live chat where we could raise any concerns both prior and during our stay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introductory weekend arranged by the international office together with the various student clubs. Again, all information was presented in a comprehensible and well organized manner.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Simply always attentive to their students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy! I am personally not on social media and I still found a place within walking distance to the University, but take your time to visit some different places before you settle down.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Visit the place before you make any further arrangements. Both to make sure that it exists, but also to get a feeling of the neighborhood. You might also ask local students of even the international office if they are familiar with the district. Afterall safety is a reasonable thing to consider.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are plenty of reasonable housing opportunities within walking distance of Campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Uniandes use two different platforms to register classes and it was simply quite disappointing how difficult it was for most exchange students. The staff in the international office is aware of the issues and try to assist all incoming students, but some had to settle with other courses than what they had wished for. Furthermore the system is rather rigid, so I recommend that any student considering Uniandes find a handful of classes to stay flexible. It is possible to sign up for more classes and withdraw or cancel some later in the process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First come first serve. In theory international students were allowed to enter the platform before the other students, but more than a few had issues with the platform not working. In that case one had to apply through another platform that for some strange reason allowed all the courses to fill up, which in a lot of cases resulted in people not getting the courses they needed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: In person, e-mail, or online call. Very service minded and helpful indeed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: First I had issues with the first platform, but I managed to convince two professors to open their class when the system would not let me register. Others were less fortunate and had to settle with something else.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Identify all the courses of your interest which could be approved at KU, ask the responsible professor to share the course description, and finally consider to apply for fewer courses with more credits in order to make your week more manageable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Excellent professors! Relevant material!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: High expectations. Not an awful lot of reading (80-100p per week per class), but compared to KU I had to write a lot of papers: In one course I had to hand in 3-4 pages every class, other than that each class had a midterm paper and a final paper of approximately 10p each. Finally, all my courses had an oral component which could for instance be a group presentation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I followed three courses which all took shape of seminars.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: CISO 4043 ; CISO 4029; CISO 4640. Two anthropological courses and a political economics class

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the anthropological courses were extremely interesting. Not only did the teachers have a lot of experience they also invited guest lecturers to join our conversations.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Taxis and robbers

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation (taxi) was cheaper than in Denmark, but Bogota is a big city where you do not want to walk after dark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Hands down the best sports facilities at Uniandes!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dance, museums, concerts, city-walks (!), cooking classes, and all sorts of clubs!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the facilities! - sign up for a free dance class or learn to swim.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Casa de la Paz in Bogota, graffiti tour, street rap, salsa clubs in Bogota... Go explore, but remember that you have time after the study program ends ! Some students seemed to burn out towards the end because they had not taken time to study.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Somewhat difficult to asses the safety situation to be honest, but besides from that people were extremely helpful and fun.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in class! Ask them out or join a student club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Safety

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People seemed genuinely curious!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do not stress but take your time to plan your study. And do not be shy to ask for help!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Uniandes is the most expensive private university in Colombia, which is reflected in the demography of the people attending class. Some would rightfully claim that it is an elitist upper class institution, so do not expect an alternative school with progressive student politics, etc. 
Teachers and students seem open to critical discussions and I did not experience any political dogmatism, nonetheless, I do recommend to visit 'La Nacional' to not leave Colombia...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: School ! No doubt.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Personal relationships in Denmark

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
